marginal_counterfactual.production_exit_interpretation: Removing the root normal edge can remove three to five package versions in consumer-style cells, depending on target and sharing.
marginal_counterfactual.dev_oracle_retention_interpretation: The four workspace-dev-build-audit cells remove zero package versions because workspace dev/test edges, including the compatibility-member dev dependency, retain the incumbent. Production exit and dev-oracle retirement are therefore separate gates.
marginal_counterfactual.no_claim: Package-count marginals do not prove source parity, behavior, performance, security, release readiness, or that the root edge may be removed.

gaps.summary: Capability registry source owners omit every production futures-lite site.
The public ecosystem Stream impls have no behavioral test.
The existing downstream fixture proves only the owned Stream trait.
Capability registry features incorrectly imply the unconditional edge is feature-gated.
Governance artifacts disagree about whether the baseline is planned or executable.
The root manifest comment describes only the two web sites and omits the other production and test surfaces.
ATP SDK types retain the foreign Stream implementations and now have source-authored owned Stream implementations, but compile, downstream ergonomics and behavioral parity evidence remain unexecuted.
The ADR census drifted from roughly 796 references in 148 src files to 817 references in 150 src files at the A1 baseline.
The ADR calls future::join_all consumed, but it is comment-only and absent from futures-lite 2.6.1; future::or is consumed but omitted.
The ATP foreign Stream impls self-wake on Empty, which can create wake churn and has no focused pending/wake test.
The ADR treats the root edge as the whole dependency story and omits the compatibility-member direct dev edge.
fuzz targets contain two stale futures-lite comments but no direct futures-lite call or manifest edge.

rollback_triggers: AtpWriter or AtpReader no longer satisfies the ecosystem Stream trait before downstream evidence approves the break
Router::handle requires an ambient runtime or changes from a synchronous entry point
signal listeners cease using runtime-independent dedicated threads
construction-phase or poll-phase web panic escapes
a helper changes poll order, wake behavior, panic propagation, Send or lifetime acceptance, or drop semantics without explicit parity evidence
a test, benchmark, example, fuzz, wasm, conformance, or compatibility Cargo profile silently loses its executor
a race migration claims loser drain while merely dropping the loser
production graph exit is conflated with dev-oracle retirement
no_claim_boundaries: This inventory does not authorize changing or removing futures-lite.
Source pins and executable probes do not prove broad workspace health, release readiness, performance parity, or live RCH fleet availability.
The occurrence census classifies textual references and Cargo-built profiles; it does not claim every reference is behaviorally covered.
The incumbent future::race and future::or drop losers; this inventory does not treat drop as project-level loser drain or quiescence.
The existing downstream fixture does not prove the public ATP ecosystem Stream journey.
Marginal package counts do not prove behavioral replacement parity.
The source-authored owned ATP Stream implementations have not been compiled or behaviorally exercised and do not authorize cutover.
No local Cargo fallback is approved when a remote-required proof lane is blocked.
